attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own post.

semantics.note: Firm 'will' with no deadline, so it is a forecast. In context, 'from the ashes' assumes the LLM scaling approach fails first; the proposition keeps his wording but leaves that assumption unstated.

contract.note: The plain reading counts any new AI method with experiments, which makes the prediction almost automatically true. That stretches it in his favour. Ordinary readers would take it to mean new approaches emerging as alternatives after the failure of LLM scaling, and that reading is not met just by publishing papers.

evidence.note: Dreamer 4 preprint (2025-09-29) is real and correctly dated. It shows a new world-model method, but it does not show new approaches rising after a collapse of the current approach.
Tiny Recursive Model paper (2025-10-06) improves on an earlier recursive model. It is genuine new research, but it does not show the predicted rise from the ashes of a failed approach.

reviews.rationale: This is a firm forecast with no deadline. The contract's reading (any new published method) trivialises the metaphor, so I marked it unfair. Under the fair reading, new approaches emerging after LLM scaling fails, the two papers show ongoing research but not that event. Nothing makes the forecast impossible, and the evidence does not settle it.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own post.

semantics.note: A compound observation: Altman failed to deliver what he promised with GPT-5, and GPT-5 was not AGI. The rhetorical 'primary mission' line is correctly left out.

contract.note: The plain reading (a material shortfall against expectations, and not AGI) is ordinary and fair. The result depends on which promises count, and Marcus did not identify them.

evidence.note: Altman's 2024 interview sets out broad expectations of improvement but no measurable target and no promise of AGI.
Launch-day report that Altman admitted GPT-5 had not reached AGI. This supports the non-AGI part only.
OpenAI's own launch page reports improvements. It is a company disclosure and weighs against a total-failure reading without settling whether the promised leap happened.
METR's independent evaluation found measurable gains on autonomous software tasks, with remaining limits. It does not settle the shortfall question.

reviews.rationale: The non-AGI part is supported: Altman himself said GPT-5 had not reached AGI. The shortfall part is not settled: no measurable promise is identified, and the evidence shows real improvements. The contract requires both parts, and the contradiction condition is not met either, so the claim as a whole is unresolved.
